findings.title: limitFunction drops all call arguments before invoking the wrapped function
findings.cause: The wrapper returned at index.js:121-124 has no rest parameter and calls function_() with no arguments, so the public wrapper no longer forwards caller-supplied values.
findings.impact: Any consumer using limitFunction with an argument-taking function receives undefined inputs at runtime even though index.d.ts exposes the returned function as (...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>.
evidence: index.d.ts:133-136 declares the returned function as (...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>.
Runtime probe printed: limitFunction-argument undefined for limitedEcho('sentinel').
findings.reproduction_or_test: const limitedEcho = limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1}); await limitedEcho('sentinel'); Expected 'sentinel'; actual undefined.

findings.title: limit.map passes undefined as the index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: index.js:108-112 gates index forwarding on Array.isArray(iterable), passing undefined for Set, iterator, generator, and other Iterable inputs.
findings.impact: The documented iterable-wide mapper index contract is broken for non-array iterables, so callers using the index to build results, keys, offsets, or stable ordering metadata get undefined values.
evidence: readme.md:78-84 says the mapper receives the item value and its index and is equivalent to Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index)).
index.d.ts:40-43 types mapperFunction as (input: Input, index: number).
Runtime probe printed: map-set-indexes [ undefined, undefined ] and map-iterator-indexes [ undefined, undefined ].
findings.reproduction_or_test: await pLimit(2).map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (_value, index) => index); Expected [0, 1]; actual [undefined, undefined].

findings.title: Options-object construction enables rejectOnClear by default
findings.cause: index.js:6-8 destructures rejectOnClear with a default of true whenever the user passes an options object.
findings.impact: pLimit({concurrency: 1}) no longer follows the documented default. Calling clearQueue() rejects pending promises with AbortError, which can unexpectedly reject Promise.all or other awaiting code that did not opt in to rejection-on-clear semantics.
evidence: readme.md:46-52 documents rejectOnClear as Type: boolean, Default: false.
index.d.ts:99-106 documents Default: false for rejectOnClear.
Runtime probe for pLimit({concurrency: 1}) printed default-options-clearQueue-pending { state: 'rejected', name: 'AbortError', message: 'This operation was aborted' }.
findings.reproduction_or_test: const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1}); const running = limit(() => delay(50)); const pending = limit(() => 'queued'); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue(); pending rejects with AbortError even though rejectOnClear was omitted.

findings.title: Falsey non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: index.js:12 validates rejectOnClear only when the value is truthy, so falsey non-booleans such as 0, an empty string, and null are accepted.
findings.impact: Invalid options are silently accepted despite the public boolean contract, making configuration mistakes difficult to detect and allowing runtime behavior to depend on JavaScript truthiness instead of the documented type.
evidence: readme.md:46-49 documents rejectOnClear as Type: boolean.
Runtime probe printed accepted: true for rejectOnClear values 0, '', and null.
findings.reproduction_or_test: pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0}); Expected TypeError for a non-boolean option; actual construction succeeds.

findings.title: Positive Infinity is rejected as a concurrency value
findings.cause: index.js:127-130 now requires Number.isInteger(concurrency), which excludes Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY.
findings.impact: Consumers that use Infinity as an unbounded/no-limit mode now get a TypeError instead of a working limiter, despite the API accepting a number minimum 1 and the committed baseline explicitly allowing Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY.
evidence: Current index.js:127-130 rejects any value that is not Number.isInteger(concurrency) && concurrency > 0.
git show HEAD:index.js showed the baseline condition accepted Number.isInteger(concurrency) || concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY.
Runtime probe printed: infinity-concurrency { accepted: false, name: 'TypeError', message: 'Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up' }.
findings.reproduction_or_test: pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY); Expected construction to succeed as in the baseline unbounded mode; actual TypeError.

commands_run: sed -n reads of index.js, test.js, readme.md, package.json, index.d.ts, and index.test-d.ts
nl -ba reads of index.js, readme.md, and index.d.ts
rg -n 'limitFunction|rejectOnClear|map|Infinity|POSITIVE_INFINITY|clearQueue|concurrency' test.js index.test-d.ts readme.md index.d.ts index.js
